cancellation_roles.description: Wire 4.1 check 8, 4.3, 4.8, spec 3.3: messages.json's payment_request_cancellation, as the shop signs it, without a label, presented with a certificate of the shop's keys (sender_cert) at a certificate of alice's wallet's keys (recipient_cert), each with its scopes changed, its permissions those Paykit's scopes need, and signed again; a certificate holding paykit_pay holds paykit_contacts too, which paykit_pay requires, and one holding paykit_request holds paykit_settlements, which paykit_request requires (spec 3.1). A cancellation's recipient holds the other role than its sender: the payer's goes from paykit_pay to paykit_request, the payee's from paykit_request to paykit_pay. accepted are the two pairings the recipient takes at check 8; refused are paykit_pay to paykit_pay and paykit_request to paykit_request, which it drops there. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

conversion_amounts.description: Spec 7.2 step 1, wire 4.4, 4.9, specs/payment-conversion.md: the amount to pay to an endpoint, payment_endpoint_identifier of the form <asset>-<rail>-<format>, whose smallest unit has fraction_digits fraction digits, for a request of requested, under rates, the request's fixed rates or the period details' rates, null for none. The rate is the asset-rail rate (usdt-polygon), else the asset-wide rate (usdt), else exactly 1 when the endpoint's asset is the requested asset; else the endpoint is unusable for conversion and amount is null. requested times the rate is computed exactly and rounded up once to the smallest unit; amount is in the endpoint's asset, normalized.

conversion_terms.description: Wire 4.4, 4.5, 4.9, specs/payment-conversion.md: the shop's messages with their conversion terms changed, signed again by the shop, each from messages.json's message base with body replaced by the body given. Requests are payment_request_required_app, which accepts btc-lightning-bolt11 only, with fixed rates: with conversion terms the requested asset is lower-case letters and digits, each rate's asset is <asset> or <asset>-<rail> of such segments, and it matches the asset, and the rail when it names one, of an accepted endpoint. Period details name payment_request_recurring (request), a usd request with per_period conversion: their rates are cross-asset only, so a bare or rail-qualified rate for the requested asset (usd, usd-polygon) makes them invalid against the request; each rate's asset is <asset> or <asset>-<rail> of lower-case letters and digits, and matches an endpoint the details or the request name (here btc-lightning-bolt11). Where a case has request_conversion, its request is payment_request_recurring with its conversion terms replaced by it, or removed where it is null: period details carry rates only for a request with per_period conversion terms. accepted are messages alice takes, at check 10 and, for period details, against their request; refused are those she drops. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

description: Every message kind as sent in v0.2 (Switch wire 4.5, wire 4): the exact JSON bytes, their BLAKE3 hash (refs, request hash), the sender app's signature over lp("pubky-switch/v1/msg", recipient identity, JSON), and the signed plaintext layout sender app ID (16) | signature (64) | u32_be(JSON length) | JSON, before zero padding. payment_request_labelled is sent by bob's hosted app under its label, and alice's acceptance of it copies the label; label_rejections holds requests a payer drops for their label; multi_protocol_senders holds messages from apps whose certificates hold another protocol's scopes; cancellation_roles holds a cancellation between certificates of each pair of roles; payee_label_senders holds the shop's period details, receipt and cancellation about a labelled request from each selling scope, which a payer takes or drops for that request's label; conversion_terms holds the shop's period details and requests with their conversion terms changed, which a payer takes or drops; conversion_amounts holds the amount a payer pays to an endpoint under a request's or period details' rates; proof_members holds alice's proofs with an extra or missing member, which a payee drops; receipt_members holds bob's receipts with the payee's metadata and reference, which a payer takes or drops; list_versions holds the shop's Private Payment Lists with a malformed version, which a payer drops.

label_rejections.description: Switch wire 5.1 checks 8 and 10, wire 4.1, 4.5, 4.6: payment_request messages a payer drops for their label, signed by bob's hosted app, whose certificate (documents.json certificates) holds only paykit_request:shop1, each messages.json's payment_request_labelled with its label changed; alice's acceptance with a label that isn't valid, which bob's apps drop; and alice's acceptances a payee app drops at check 8 because its certificate (recipient_cert) doesn't hold their label: messages.json's payment_request_acceptance_labelled (label shop1) at an app holding only paykit_request:shop2, the hosted certificate with scopes changed and permissions derived, and the same acceptance without its label at the hosted app, which holds only paykit_request:shop1. A payer's reply with a label needs paykit_request or paykit_request:<label> for that label at the recipient; one without needs paykit_request. reason is the prototype's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

list_versions.description: Wire 4.13: the shop's private_payment_list with its version replaced by a malformed one and signed again by the shop; every other member is the list's. A version is an object with generation and counter, each 1 through 9007199254740991. A payer drops each at check 10. reason is paykit-lib's wording.

messages.name: payment_request

messages.name: payment_request_required_app
messages.note: Request without a destination, payable only to the named payee app's endpoints.

messages.name: payment_request_recurring
messages.note: Monthly request anchored on January 31; later periods get their destination from period details.

messages.name: payment_request_acceptance
messages.note: Acceptance of the one-time request; refs name the request.

messages.name: payment_request_rejection
messages.note: Rejection with the optional v0.1 reason.

messages.name: payment_request_cancellation
messages.note: Payee cancellation of the recurring request.

messages.name: payment_period_details
messages.note: Destination and rates for the February period (anchor Jan 31, clamped to Feb 28).

messages.name: payment_proof
messages.note: Proof of the one-time request's attempt.

messages.name: payment_proof_period
messages.note: Payment of the February period by alice's wallet, in btc at the period details' rate (a manual payment: an Allowance pays only requests in its own asset); refs name the request and the period details it used.

messages.name: private_payment_list
messages.note: Private Payment List with one single-use and one reusable endpoint; version is the pair of the publishing identity generation 1 and counter 12; expires_at 30 days after publishing (wire 4.13).

messages.name: payment_proof_unrequested
messages.note: Proof of a payment without a request, to the single-use list endpoint; no refs.

messages.name: payment_receipt
messages.note: Receipt for the one-time proof; refs name the proof, then the request.

messages.name: resend_request
messages.note: Ask for messages the sender's inbox accepted at one entry's acceptance time.

messages.name: resend_request_ids
messages.note: Ask for messages by msg_id.

messages.name: private_payment_list_request
messages.note: Ask the shop app for a newer list than the used one.

messages.name: allowance_proposal
messages.note: Allowee-authored proposal; terms as specs/allowances.md.

messages.name: allowance_acceptance
messages.note: Acceptance by the allower's executor app; executor_app_id is informational.

messages.name: allowance_rejection
messages.note: Rejection of another proposal (refs name that proposal).

messages.name: allowance_end
messages.note: End of the accepted Allowance; refs name the proposal and the acceptance.

messages.name: executor_notice
messages.note: Between own apps: the phone app ended the Allowance and tells the executor.

messages.name: resend_request_period
messages.note: Ask for the February period's messages of the recurring request: request_hashes names the request, billing_period the period, so the request itself isn't re-sent (wire 4.12).

messages.name: payment_request_labelled
messages.note: One-time request from bob's hosted app, which holds only paykit_request:shop1: it carries the signed label shop1, so the payer's replies go only to bob's apps holding paykit_request or paykit_request:shop1 (wire 4.5).

messages.name: payment_request_acceptance_labelled

multi_protocol_senders.description: Wire 4.1 check 8, spec 3.2, 3.3, Switch wire 3.1 "Several protocols": messages.json's payment_request and resend_request_ids, as the shop signs them, each presented with a certificate of the shop's keys that holds another protocol's scope, chat (sender_cert, documents.json multi_protocol_certificates), at alice's wallet (recipient_app), whose certificate is its certificate of documents.json certificates. Another protocol's scopes, and the switch permissions they bring, authorize no Paykit message: each kind still needs its Paykit scope, and a resend_request needs a Paykit App, one holding at least one Paykit scope. accepted are messages the wallet takes at check 8, from the shop holding paykit_request, with the paykit_settlements and paykit_contacts it requires, beside chat; refused are those it drops there, from the shop holding chat alone, a certificate Paykit's verifiers take. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

payee_label_senders.description: Spec 3.3, 3.4, wire 4.1 check 8, 4.8, 4.9, 4.11, 5.3: the shop's messages as messages.json signs them, with the refs changed to name request, presented with a certificate of the shop's keys holding sender_scope and the paykit_settlements and paykit_contacts it requires (sender_cert). request is payment_request_labelled for the receipt and the cancellation; request_recurring, messages.json's payment_request_recurring with label shop1 sent by the hosted app, or payment_request_recurring itself, unlabelled, for the period details; null for a private_payment_list and a receipt naming no request, which names payment_proof_unrequested. The receipt about a request confirms proof: messages.json's payment_proof naming payment_request_labelled and copying its label. Each passes check 10, and the details are valid against their request (wire 4.9). accepted are those the payer takes, from paykit_request and from the request's label. refused are those it drops: about a request, from another label or from a label about an unlabelled request, which pass check 8 and are dropped where the payer reads the request, a payer request record holding such a receipt or cancellation being invalid; and a private_payment_list or a receipt naming no request from a labelled scope, dropped at check 8. reason is paykit-lib's wording.

receipt_members.description: Wire 4.11: bob's receipts, payment_receipt as the shop signs it, with members added and signed again by the shop. A receipt may carry the payee's metadata, an object, as v0.1 Receipt.metadata; and a receipt of a payment without a request, whose refs name its proof alone (here payment_proof_unrequested, with that proof's attempt_id), may carry the payee's payment_reference for it. accepted are receipts a payer takes at check 10: the request's receipt with metadata, and the receipt of the payment without a request with metadata and a payment_reference. refused are receipts it drops there: the request's receipt carrying a payment_reference, whose request's reference applies, one whose metadata isn't an object, and a receipt naming a Billing Period without a request. reason is paykit-lib's wording.
